subject: Discovery follow-up: scheduling demo / rotating time slots
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Sara Li <sara.li@fintechco.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Jul 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery follow-up: scheduling demo / rotating time slots

Hi Sara —

Thanks again for taking the time today — great discussion getting a sense of FinTech Co's priority use cases for embeddings + real-time inference. Per our call, next best step would be a technical deep dive / demo with your engineering leads so we can walk through integration patterns and latency/cost expectations.

Because your team spans US, EU and APAC, we suggest a rotating demo cadence so the same week-to-week meeting alternates times to share burden across time zones. Proposed options (all are 60-min technical demos + 15 min for Q&A):

- Option A (rotation week 1):
  - US-friendly: Tue 10:00 PDT / Tue 13:00 EDT / Tue 18:00 BST
- Option B (rotation week 2):
  - EU-friendly: Thu 16:00 BST / Thu 17:00 CEST / Thu 11:00 EDT
- Option C (rotation week 3):
  - APAC-friendly: Mon 09:00 SGT / Mon 01:00 BST (overnight EU) / Sun 16:00 PDT

If you'd prefer a fixed single time instead of rotation, we can do that as well — just let us know constraints (max 2 AM local is tough for anyone).

Quick asks:
- Who from your engineering org should be invited (names + emails)?
- Any specific topics you want covered beyond the integration + perf/cost questions (e.g., KV cache, private deployment, custom model variants)?

I've attached the call notes from today's discovery and a short timezone playbook we use when coordinating multi-region demos. If helpful I can also share a calendar polling link.

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0192
Attachment: discovery-notes.pdf

From: Sara Li <sara.li@fintechco.com>

Date: Wed, 14 Jul 2026 23:05:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Discovery follow-up: scheduling demo / rotating time slots

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the follow-up and the clear options. Really helpful.

Quick context — our engineering group that needs to attend includes:
- Tom Becker (backend lead) <t.becker@fintechco.com> — mainly US/EU hours
- Min-Jae Park (ML infra) <m.park@fintechco.com> — APAC-based (SG/KST)
- Lena Ortiz (security/compliance) <lena.ortiz@fintechco.com> — EU

Rotation sounds fair. I'm leaning toward starting with Option B (EU-friendly) this week since Lena needs to be present for the segment on data retention and our private deployment questions. For the follow-up, we can rotate to an APAC-friendly time the next week.

Two requests:
1) Can you confirm the expected agenda and timeboxed segments (we have a strict 75-minute window max)?
2) Could you send a single calendar poll with the three rotation options so I can loop in Tom and Min-Jae?

I'll check with the team on conflicts; Min-Jae flagged that anything past 22:00 SGT is tricky but doable once per month.

\u000Farai
Sara Li
Head of Product, FinTech Co
sara.li@fintechco.com

Date: Thu, 15 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery follow-up: scheduling demo / rotating time slots

Hi Sara — looping in to help coordinate logistics and propose a single poll/calendar with rotating slots.

Below is a compact schedule we can drop into a calendar poll (each option is a 75-min block; first 60 minutes demo + 15 Q&A/security deep-dive):

- Option 1 (US-focused week):
  - Tue 2026-07-20 10:00 PDT / Tue 13:00 EDT / Tue 18:00 BST (good for Tom)
- Option 2 (EU-focused week):
  - Thu 2026-07-22 16:00 BST / Thu 17:00 CEST / Thu 11:00 EDT (suggested for this week)
- Option 3 (APAC-focused week):
  - Mon 2026-07-26 09:00 SGT / Sun 2026-07-25 16:00 PDT / Mon 01:00 BST (overnight EU)

Notes:
- We can set a rotating cadence: Week A -> Option 1, Week B -> Option 2, Week C -> Option 3, then repeat. That minimizes repeated night calls for any one region.
- Agenda (timeboxed):
  - 0-10 min: intros & objectives
  - 10-30 min: integration architecture (APIs, SDKs, sample code)
  - 30-50 min: perf and cost expectations (batching, caching, quant profiles)
  - 50-65 min: security/compliance Q&A (data residency, logs, SOC2 items)
  - 65-75 min: next steps / mutual action items

I'll put these three options into a Calendly poll and share the link by end of day. Also attaching a short timezone-sales-pack with quick local time equivalents so you can forward to the group.

Thanks —
Aditya Rao
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.com
Attachment: timezone-sales-pack.pdf
